title: Maximum Number of Consecutive Values You Can Make
statement:
You own a pile of coins; `coins[i]` is the value of the i-th coin, and several coins may share a value. A total `x` counts as *reachable* when some selection of your coins, each used at most once, adds up to exactly `x`; picking no coins at all reaches `0`.

Return the length of the longest run of reachable integers that begins at `0`: the largest `k` such that every one of `0, 1, ..., k - 1` is reachable.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every subset is hopeless for thousands of coins. Instead, grow a run of reachable totals. Suppose every total in `0 .. reach - 1` is reachable. Adding a coin worth `coin` makes `coin .. coin + reach - 1` reachable too. If `coin <= reach`, that new range touches or overlaps the old one, so the run extends to `0 .. reach + coin - 1`. If `coin > reach`, the total `reach` cannot be made: the smaller coins add up to at most `reach - 1`, and every remaining coin is too large on its own. Taking coins in increasing order means the first coin that leaves a gap ends the search.

## Approach

1. Sort `coins` in increasing order.
2. Start with `reach = 1`: only total `0` is known to be reachable.
3. For each `coin` in order, stop if `coin > reach`, because total `reach` can never be formed.
4. Otherwise extend the run with `reach += coin`.
5. Return `reach`, the count of totals `0 .. reach - 1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`coins = [1, 3]` is already sorted. `reach` starts at `1`. Coin `1` is not bigger than `1`, so `reach` becomes `2` (totals 0 and 1). Coin `3` is bigger than `2`: total `2` cannot be made, so the loop stops and the answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) extra beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Start `reach` at `1`, not `0`: the empty selection already makes total `0`, and the answer counts it.
- The test is `coin > reach`, not `coin > reach - 1`; a coin equal to `reach` fills the next total exactly.
- Without sorting, an early large coin would end the scan even though small coins later could fill the gap.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `reach` | every total from `0` to `reach - 1` is reachable; also the answer so far |
| `coin` | the current coin in increasing order |

narration.2: Sort the coins so the smallest ones extend the run first.
narration.3: Only total 0 is reachable at the start, so the run has length 1.
narration.5: Visit the coins from smallest to largest.
narration.6: A coin bigger than reach leaves total reach impossible to form.
narration.7: Every later coin is at least as big, so stop here.
narration.9: Otherwise the coin shifts the whole run up and joins it, extending the run by coin.
narration.11: Totals 0 through reach - 1 are all reachable; return how many there are.
